summary: I independently reviewed all 38 owned units (the s0077 memorial, s0220–s0251, the s0078 letter and s0252–s0255), all 51 owned items and all 24 owned people against the Chinese text, Jinshu 7 and ZZTJ vol.96. 49 items are supported: Yu Liang's AD 340 death and his 327–328 provocation of Su Jun and Zu Yue, Yu Yi's AD 340 succession, Empress Dowager Yu's AD 328 death, Emperor Cheng of Jin's 340–341 receipt of the memorial, and the 17 Han and pre-Han exempla, which are correctly modelled as retrospective references dated to the 340–341 memorial and letter with empty hints. Two items (and person p084) share one defect that blocks approval: claim-504 and hints-p084 give Yu Bing a point year of AD 340, but ZZTJ places his ministerial succession in AD 339, and his attested role as addressee and respondent falls in the 340–341 window ending with the AD 341 grant. I found no omitted births, deaths or ages in the owned units. The packet supplied only English (en); the literal translation field was unavailable and is unchecked. One English chronology defect, in s0233, is reported separately. This is not full-chapter or publication approval.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang's own death, reported in s0077 as news reaching Murong Huang.
itemChecks.reason: s0077 explicitly reports 庾亮薨; Jinshu 7 dates it to Xiankang 6, first month, day gengzi (AD 340), so the year-precision attestation is correct. It repeats the death notice rather than recording separate activity.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang's governing as chief maternal uncle and his slighting of frontier generals, which provoked Su Jun and Zu Yue's revolt.
itemChecks.reason: s0232 makes Yu Liang's provocation the cause of the Su Jun–Zu Yue revolt. Jinshu 7 dates the outbreak to Xianhe 2, eleventh month (AD 327), and the capital's fall to Xianhe 3 (AD 328), so a 327–328 window is a supported uncertainty window.

輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang's own death.
itemChecks.reason: s0077 states 庾亮薨. Jinshu 7 gives 六年春正月庚子 under Xiankang, which is AD 340 (the first month falls in Feb–Mar 340), so a year-precision death of AD 340 is supported.

itemChecks.event: Yu Bing's own attested position as chief minister, addressee of Huang's memorial and letter, and his response with He Chong.
itemChecks.reason: The point year 340 is false precision. Yu Bing's succession as minister (繼為相) happened in Xiankang 5 (AD 339), when ZZTJ vol.96 makes him Director of the Secretariat after Wang Dao died. The memorial, the letter and his alarmed joint memorial with He Chong fall in the 340–341 window (the memorial and letter, which s0077 places after Yu Liang's death (Xiankang 6, first month, AD 340) and which ZZTJ vol.96 sets in the lead-up to the Xiankang 7 (AD 341) King of Yan grant).

evidence.quote: 而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機

itemChecks.event: Yu Yi's own succession to Yu Liang's generalship.
itemChecks.reason: s0077 says Yu Yi succeeded as general after Yu Liang's death. ZZTJ vol.96 (Xiankang 6, first month, day gengxu) names Yu Yi Chief Controller of six provinces and Inspector of Jing to replace Yu Liang at Wuchang, so a point year of AD 340 is supported.

itemChecks.event: Emperor Cheng of Jin's receipt, as the addressee, of Murong Huang's memorial, ending in the grant he approved.
itemChecks.reason: The 陛下 of the memorial is Emperor Cheng (died AD 342). The memorial follows Yu Liang's death in AD 340, and Jinshu 7 dates the grant of the Yan seal to Xiankang 7, second month (AD 341), so the 340–341 window is supported uncertainty.

evidence.quote: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道

itemChecks.event: Su Jun's own revolt, driven by rage at Yu Liang, which brought ruin on the state.
itemChecks.reason: Jinshu 7 dates the revolt of Zu Yue and Su Jun to Xianhe 2, eleventh month (AD 327). Su Jun took the capital in Xianhe 3 (AD 328) and was killed in its ninth month, so the 327–328 window is bounded by his own revolt and death.

evidence.quote: 故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國

itemChecks.event: Zu Yue's own revolt, driven by rage at Yu Liang, which brought ruin on the state.
itemChecks.reason: Jinshu 7 lists Zu Yue first among the rebels in Xianhe 2, eleventh month (AD 327). The 敗國 (fall of the capital) came in Xianhe 3 (AD 328). His later flight is outside this event, so the 327–328 window fits the attested rage-to-ruin event.

evidence.quote: 故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國

findings.problem: claim-504 dates Yu Bing's attestation to a point year of AD 340 from 又聞庾亮薨, and the hint copies it. His succession as minister (中書監) was in Xiankang 5 (AD 339, ZZTJ vol.96). findings.action: Replace claim-504's westernYear AD 340 with westernInterval AD 340–341. Keep the sourceDate 又聞庾亮薨 and the event as Yu Bing holding power as the memorial's and letter's addressee and respondent. Set hints-p084 to ["AD 340-341"]. Do not choose a single year inside the window.

references.reason: Anchor for Yu Liang's death, the Yu brothers' succession and the start of Murong Huang's memorial.

references.quote: 輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國
references.reason: Links Yu Liang's provocation to the 327–328 revolt of Su Jun and Zu Yue.

references.quote: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐
references.reason: Records the Empress Dowager's indignant death, which Jinshu 7 dates to AD 328.

references.quote: 而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機
references.reason: Shows Yu Bing holding power at the time of the memorial (the 340–341 window).
